key_insight: TRACE uses a concept bottleneck model to make longitudinal glioblastoma response classification more interpretable by predicting clinically meaningful tumor concepts before the final label.
clinical_relevance: This could support MRI response assessment in a way that is easier for clinicians to inspect, verify, and correct than direct end-to-end prediction.
method: Pairs baseline and follow-up 3D multimodal MRI scans with a shared vision encoder.
Predicts root tumor measurements, then derives RANO-style concepts through deterministic rules.
Adds scan interval and new-lesion information as passthrough concepts for final 4-class response prediction.
evidence_signal: On 5-fold patient-wise cross-validation in the LUMIERE dataset, TRACE achieved macro F1 of 0.4769 for 4-class response and 0.7085 for binary progression vs non-progression.
watch_item: The approach still needs larger protocol-aligned datasets and external validation before clinical use.
paper_title: TRACE: A Concept Bottleneck Model for Longitudinal 3D Glioblastoma Response Assessment
